Control study · Identity → registrable assets

Your Name Is Not Necessarily Yours

Your name can be your identity, your reputation, a trademark, a company asset, a domain, a social handle, and an archive authority—and those forms of control do not automatically travel together.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

The label may bear a founder’s name while contracts, registrations, accounts, voting arrangements, or a later transaction place key forms of control elsewhere. “It is my name” is therefore the beginning of an inventory, not the end of the analysis.

WIPO distinguishes the intellectual-property tools that may operate around fashion, including trademarks and industrial designs; its fashion diagnostic is an educational starting point rather than a legal conclusion. The useful editorial move is to separate the asset layers, identify the evidence for each, and mark where qualified counsel must replace inference.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · NAME

Which identity is being used?

List the personal name, legal entity names, label names, collection marks, monograms, product names, likeness, signatures, and recurring verbal identifiers separately.

PROPOSALS28S29

02 · CHANNEL

Where does the public encounter it?

Domains, storefronts, social handles, marketplaces, mailing lists, apps, authentication systems, and press accounts each have different administrators and recovery paths.

PROPOSALS29S32

03 · RIGHT

What kind of control is claimed?

Trademark, copyright, industrial-design protection, patent, contract, publicity or personality rights, corporate control, and platform access answer different questions. One cannot be substituted casually for another.

VERIFIEDS28S30S31

04 · EVIDENCE

What record would prove it?

Registration records, assignments, licenses, operating agreements, access logs, vendor accounts, and executed contracts belong in a control map with owner, territory, term, renewal, and review fields.

PROPOSALS29S32

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

This exhibition is an issue-spotting tool, not legal advice. Public databases can reveal registrations and recorded assignments, but they do not necessarily establish every contractual, common-law, territorial, or beneficial interest.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Inventory every public-facing form of the founder or house name.
  2. Record the legal or account owner for each—never infer from the display name.
  3. Add territory, class or category, term, renewal date, administrator, and recovery path.
  4. Send unresolved ownership or licensing questions to qualified counsel.
